Article Title: SC directs Andhra Pradesh poll panel to decide on extending nomination deadline by Thursday
Article Text:
SC asks Andhra poll panel to decide on extending nomination deadline by tomorrow

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday directed the Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission to decide by Thursday whether to extend nomination deadlines for urban local body polls in areas where candidates were allegedly prevented from filing nominations due to law and order issues.The court asked the poll panel to defer publication of the final candidates’ list until October 25 and examine complaints of violence and obstruction by tomorrow. If the commission decides to extend the deadline, candidates must get at least 48 hours from the publication of the decision to file nominations.The court also ordered police protection and CCTV coverage at nomination centres and sought a compliance report. The matter will be heard next on October 27.(With inputs from ANI)
Article Summary: SC asks Andhra poll panel to decide on extending nomination deadline by tomorrow. If the commission decides to extend the deadline, candidates must get at least 48 hours from the publication of the decision to file nominations. Court also ordered police protection and CCTV coverage at nomination centres and sought a compliance report.

Article Title: ‘Doing a real disservice’: Annamalai backs CJP leaders, questions their continued custody
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Former Tamil Nadu BJP president K Annamalai on Tuesday expressed Cockroach Janata Party and questioned Delhi Police's handling of the case against its leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka.While talking to reporters, Annamalai said that continued judicial custody of CJP leaders raises concerns about the rule of law."I'm a little bit concerned in our country. I have a feeling they (Delhi Police) have taken the law into their hands, and the judge gets recused... I may not agree with many of the CJP's modes of protest. I may not agree with some of the antics of CJP. That's a different argument. But I completely support CJP in terms of the questions they want to raise."It is for the government to answer. But to arrest them for a violation and again to drag them in terms of how they spend their time in jail, that is only going to make the leaders of CJP stronger. I'm afraid of saying that the Delhi police are doing a real disservice," he added.He also said that Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi has every right to question the SIR process, but institutional damage should not be caused."Rahul Gandhi has every right to question the SIR process, but institutional damage should not be caused," he further said.Earlier on Monday, a Delhi court extended the CJP leaders' judicial custody by two days for allegedly entering Jantar Mantar, which is no longer a designated protest venue, and obstructing police personnel on duty.Along with other CJP workers, they waved the national flag at the site and raised slogans against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar before being detained and placed under preventive custody.According to their lawyer, their bail sureties were rejected due to a reported mismatch in documents. They will now be produced before the court on Wednesday.Meanwhile, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership and praised Das and Ranka for remaining defiant despite spending five days in judicial custody."You must be feeling very strong keeping a 26-year-old Saurav Das in jail. You must be feeling very strong beating children on the streets. You must be feeling very strong putting up barricades across Delhi and dragging students on the streets," he said.Dipke claimed that Das and Ranka had gone to Jantar Mantar to wave the national flag but were sent to judicial custody. He also alleged that their court hearings had been repeatedly postponed. "Is this strength? Hiding behind the police, hiding behind the courts, is this Narendra Modi's strength?" he asked.
Article Summary: Former Tamil Nadu BJP president K Annamalai questioned Delhi Police's handling of the case against CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. He also said that Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi has every right to question the SIR process, but institutional damage should not be caused.

Article Title: Hours after custody extension, Delhi Police transfers CJP leaders' trespassing case to crime branch
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Monday transferred the trespassing case against Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das to the crime branch, news agency ANI reported, citing sources.This came hours after a Delhi court extended the CJP leaders' judicial custody by two days for allegedly entering Jantar Mantar, which is no longer a designated protest venue, and obstructing police personnel on duty.Along with other CJP workers, they waved the national flag at the site and raised slogans against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar before being detained and placed under preventive custody.According to their lawyer, their bail sureties were rejected due to a reported mismatch in documents. They will now be produced before the court on Wednesday."Today, when we reached the court, the five-day custody period had ended. On the last date of hearing, the court had stated that it did not find the sureties legitimate enough to be accepted. Today, we produced fresh sureties and brought them to court. When our matter was taken up, the State filed a fresh application, which was served on us at that point.In this application, they sought a further five to seven days of judicial custody," the CJP leaders' advocate said."The reasons they gave were absolutely shocking to us. They claimed there was an imminent threat to public order and public tranquillity and that, therefore, the accused needed to remain in judicial custody... It is very unfortunate, and everyone must remember that there is currently no FIR against my clients in connection with this issue. This concerns preventive custody. They have been detained out of fear that they might go and protest. There is no FIR, no pending case against them in this matter, and no investigation for which they need to be questioned. This is absolutely appalling and deeply disturbing. I cannot remember the last time people were kept in preventive custody under such circumstances. We will pursue the matter legally, but this has been hugely disappointing for all of us," he added.The development came amid allegations by the CJP that the bail proceedings had been deliberately delayed to prevent the release of its two convenors, who were sent to five-day judicial custody on October 13 following a protest at Jantar Mantar.On Sunday, the special executive magistrate hearing their bail matter claimed that unknown persons were threatening him, following which the police registered a non-cognisable report.Meanwhile, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership and praised Das and Ranka for remaining defiant despite spending five days in judicial custody."You must be feeling very strong keeping a 26-year-old Saurav Das in jail. You must be feeling very strong beating children on the streets. You must be feeling very strong putting up barricades across Delhi and dragging students on the streets," he said.Dipke claimed that Das and Ranka had gone to Jantar Mantar to wave the national flag but were sent to judicial custody. He also alleged that their court hearings had been repeatedly postponed. "Is this strength? Hiding behind the police, hiding behind the courts, is this Narendra Modi's strength?" he asked.
Article Summary: Delhi Police transfer trespassing case against Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das to crime branch. Delhi court extends CJP leaders' judicial custody by two days for allegedly entering Jantar Mantar, which is no longer a designated protest venue.

Article Title: 'Too tired of spreading lies’: BJP claims Rahul on Vietnam trip; Congress hits back
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Tuesday stepped up its attack on Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi over his alleged foreign trip amid the opposition’s protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The BJP shared a video on X purportedly showing Rahul Gandhi aboard a flight to Vietnam.“Too tired of spreading lies. Let me tour Vietnam for a while, who would get to know,” the BJP said.BJP leader Shahnawaz Hussain also took a swipe at Rahul Gandhi, saying he needed to rest after causing inconvenience to people in the country.“Rahul ji was very tired. He worked very hard. Sometimes he went to a police station, sometimes he sat inside All India Radio, sometimes he lay down on the road to get his pictures clicked, sometimes he pushed and shoved police personnel, and sometimes he knocked a journalist to the ground. He works so hard that he gets exhausted,” Hussain said.“After all this hard work, Rahul needs rest. Every time he puts in such hard work, he takes rest afterwards. So, he has gone to relax, and there should be no disturbance to his rest. He wants to cause inconvenience to the people of the country and then relax himself. The youth of the country are watching closely. He makes all kinds of claims here about the voices of students and the voices of young people, and now this ‘voice’ has reached Vietnam as well,” he added.Meanwhile, Congress hit back at the BJP, accusing it of making an unnecessary issue out of Rahul Gandhi’s foreign trips.“Who travels where and when... what is the issue? Do others not travel abroad? Rahul Gandhi is an individual and the leader of the opposition. He has his duties. He interacts with students at Yale University, meets students in London and engages with intellectuals there. He even gives press interviews, something the Prime Minister does not do,” Congress leader Sandeep Dikshit said.Dikshit also cited Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s foreign visits during Parliament sessions to counter the BJP’s criticism.“We also have a tradition that the Prime Minister does not travel abroad when the Lok Sabha is in session. But our PM broke that tradition. Why does no question arise at that time?” he asked.Rahul Gandhi has been leading the opposition’s campaign against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the SIR of electoral rolls, demanding his resignation. The Election Commission and the BJP have rejected allegations of irregularities in the revision exercise, accusing Gandhi of “spreading lies”.
Article Summary: BJP leader Shahnawaz Hussain also took a swipe at Rahul Gandhi, saying he needed to rest after causing inconvenience to people in the country. Congress hit back at the BJP, accusing it of making an unnecessary issue out of Rahul Gandhi’s foreign trips.

Article Title: ‘Thank you for free publicity’: Dipke on cockroach effigy being burnt alongside Ravan on Dussehra
Article Text:
Shri Keshav Ramlila Committee is set to burn the cockroach effigy alongside the traditional effigies of Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Meghnad at its grounds in Pitampura.

What has the committee said?

How did ‘cockroach’ become a political name?

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder, Abhijeet Dipke, on Monday took a sarcastic dig at the planned burning of a 30-foot-tall cockroach effigy alongside Ravan during Dussehra celebrations on October 20 in Delhi, saying, “Thank you for the free publicity. ”The Shri Keshav Ramlila Committee is set to burn the cockroach effigy alongside the traditional effigies of Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Meghnad at its grounds in Pitampura. The preparation for the event is underway, with the committee saying the initiative is intended to spread awareness about cleanliness and unhygienic conditions.Ashok Goel Devaraha, president of the Shri Keshav Ramlila Committee and BJP MLA from Model Town, said the cockroach effigy was meant to symbolise filth and reinforce the message of the triumph of good over evil.Devaraha told ANI that the committee had previously burnt effigies representing issues such as Naxalism and terrorism. This year, it chose a cockroach to highlight the need to eliminate dirt and unhygienic conditions from homes, neighbourhoods and society.He also denied that the decision was politically motivated, saying the initiative aligned with the Swachh Bharat and Swachh Delhi campaigns.The planned effigy comes amid the rise of the satirical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a movement that emerged following remarks by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant during a Supreme Court hearing on May 15.The CJI had compared certain individuals with fraudulent degrees who become social media or RTI activists to “cockroaches” attacking the system.The remarks triggered a backlash among young people and inspired the CJP movement. The CJI later said his oral remarks had been “misquoted” and used with “malicious intent”.The CJP has since staged protests against former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and is now demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Article Summary: The Shri Keshav Ramlila Committee is set to burn the cockroach effigy alongside the traditional effigies of Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Meghnad. The preparation for the event is underway, with the committee saying the initiative is intended to spread awareness about cleanliness and unhygienic conditions.

Article Title: Congress snubbed delimitation talks: Government signals Parliament session
Article Text:
It was not clear why the demand for consultation was being made repeatedly, Rijiju said

NEW DELHI: Days after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge called for an all-party meeting to discuss any fresh delimitation proposal, govt on Monday said it had already consulted many opposition parties, including Samajwadi Party, DMK and NCP (SP), and could not hold talks with Congress because of its own unwillingness, refuelling the buzz that Parliament may be called for a short duration to take up the legislation.In a sharp response to Kharge's Oct 16 letter to PM Narendra Modi, parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said, "When after repeated requests Congress didn't give dates for discussion, govt's outreach extended to other political parties. Consultations were held with representatives of parties including SP, DMK, YSRCP, NCP (SP), Shiv Sena (UBT), AIMIM and BJD with a view to building a broader consensus in support of the proposed legislation. "Also Read: Dushyant Kumar Gautam sworn in as Sikkim governor, Congress vows stir In these circumstances, it was not clear why the demand for consultation was being made repeatedly, he added, rejecting Kharge's suggestion. Rijiju sought to give the impression of Congress's isolation over the issue by emphasising govt's consultations with other key members of the opposition in contrast to both Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, not giving him any date for discussion when he had met them during the last session.Writing to Modi, Kharge had also questioned the "unprecedented" delay in proroguing the monsoon session, which was adjourned indefinitely on Aug 13. Dismissing his contention, Rijiju cited precedents and underlined that no constitutional requirement existed prescribing a specific period within which a House must be prorogued following its adjournment sine die."The mere fact that a House has not been prorogued does not, by itself, give rise to any constitutional or procedural impropriety or irregularity," Rijiju said. — Kumar Rakesh

Article Title: Dushyant Kumar Gautam sworn in as Sikkim governor, Congress vows stir
Article Text:
Dushyant Kumar Gautam was sworn in as the 19th governor of Sikkim Monday, succeeding Om Prakash Mathur.

GANGTOK/DELHI: Dushyant Kumar Gautam was sworn in as the 19th governor of Sikkim Monday, succeeding Om Prakash Mathur.Slamming the governing BJP for sticking with Gautam's appointment as governor despite the shadow of a murder case, Congress said its protest over the issue will intensify and it will gherao the Uttarakhand assembly on Oct 27.AICC's Uttarakhand in-charge Kumari Selja said it is shameful that a person whose name is linked to a massive scandal is being appointed to Raj Bhavan. "Every citizen in Uttarakhand feels that there is no justice in the state. The murder of the young woman in the hill state in 2022 had shaken the country, but justice has not been meted out to this day." Selja said the party will take out yatras all over the state to highlight the issue.Gautam was administered the oath of office and secrecy by Sikkim HC chief justice A Muhamed Mustaque in the presence of CM Prem Singh Tamang, judges and others.
Article Summary: Dushyant Kumar Gautam was sworn in as the 19th governor of Sikkim Monday. He succeeds Om Prakash Mathur. Congress slams the governing BJP for sticking with GautAm's appointment. Congress said its protest over the issue will intensify and it will gherao the Uttarakhand assembly.

Article Title: Ludhiana school horror: Peon gropes, kisses 16-year-old student in office, records video
Article Text:
A school peon in Ludhiana has been arrested for allegedly molesting a 16-year-old student





LUDHIANA: A school peon has been arrested for molesting a 16-year-old student inside the premises. The complaint also alleges that the accused recorded a video of the girl.The Tibba police have registered a case against the accused under Section 75 of BNS and relevant provisions of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.According to the complaint filed by the girl’s mother, her daughter needed a book for school and had approached her class teacher about it. The teacher reportedly asked her to collect the book from the teacher’s office.The girl’s mother alleged that when her daughter entered the office to look for the book, the accused who worked as a peon at the school, arrived there. While the student was searching for the book, the accused allegedly grabbed her, pinned her against a wall, kissed her and subjected her to inappropriate acts against her will.The complainant further alleged that the family later learned that the accused had also recorded a video of the student.ASI Ravinder Kumar, who is investigating the case, stated that soon after receiving the complaint the police arrested the accused.
Article Summary: A school peon has been arrested for molesting a 16-year-old student inside the premises. The complaint also alleges that the accused recorded a video of the girl. The Tibba police have registered a case against the accused under Section 75 of BNS.

Article Title: Video of ASI sexually harassing volunteer at Kolkata puja pandal goes viral; cop arrested
Article Text:
An Assistant Sub-Inspector of West Bengal Police has been arrested for allegedly sexually harassing a volunteer





KOLKATA: An Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) of the West Bengal Police has been arrested for allegedly sexually harassing a woman volunteer on duty at Suruchi Sangha during Durga Puja , after a video purportedly showing the incident circulated on social media.The accused, identified as Kabirul Hasan Mondal (50), an ASI (Armed) attached to the 3rd Battalion's 'B' Company of the Kolkata Armed Police (KAP), was arrested following a written complaint lodged by the 21-year-old volunteer.According to the complaint, the alleged incident took place between 11pm and 11.30pm on October 17 at the exit gate of Suruchi Sangha, where the woman was performing duty during Durga Puja.The complainant alleged that the ASI made unwelcome physical contact with her, amounting to sexual harassment.Police registered a case at New Alipore police station on October 18 under Section 75(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The accused's family members have been informed of his arrest.
Article Summary: Kabirul Hasan Mondal (50), an ASI (Armed), was arrested following a written complaint lodged by the 21-year-old volunteer. The alleged incident took place between 11pm and 11.30pm on October 17 at the exit gate of Suruchi Sangha, where the woman was performing duty during Durga Puja.

KOLATHUR: VCK leader Thol Thirumavalavan claimed that DMK leader and former chief minister MK Stalin suffered an electoral defeat in the Kolathur constituency due to mass voter deletions carried out during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.Speaking at a joint demonstration organised by the INDIA bloc against the Election Commission of India (ECI) and the implementation of SIR, Thirumavalavan accused the BJP of weaponising the revision process to target political rivals. Article Title: Will not let farmers face a black Diwali, oppn bloc anti-democracy: Eknath Shinde
Article Text:
Calling the INDIA bloc Ravana, Shiv Sena chief Eknath Shinde said it is anti-democracy

Mumbai:





Dedicating Shiv Sena ’s annual Dussehra rally on Tuesday to the state’s drought-affected farmers, deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde said the state govt and his party are firmly behind them and will not let them face a black Diwali.“Farmers have the greatest right over the state’s treasury. We will ensure they receive relief and the Rs 5,000 interim payout. Many trucks full of ration have already been dispatched. They should not lose hope,” said Shinde, addressing his party at the Nesco ground in Goregaon.He said farmers have the first right over him and he will work for them “till the last drop of my blood”. He said Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah had also ensured their strong support to the state’s farmers.He asked shiv sainiks to work 24x7 to ensure farmers receive help and to go to fields with saffron flags on their shoulders. “We are giving 25,000 sewing machines and cycles to women. Now, we will organise mass weddings for the children of farmers,” he said. He also claimed that the state had provided Rs 60,000 crore to farmers.Shinde said the opposition is jealous of him, whether he was in London or on a visit to a village.“Whether I speak in Marathi or English in the British parliament or go to London, Delhi or a village, they get a stomach ache,” he said in a likely dig at Shiv Sena (UBT). He was referring to the Commonwealth Public Leadership Award and the Statesmanship Award he received in the UK last month.Criticising the opposition for protests against alleged vote theft, he said, “The biggest vote theft was in 2019 when [undivided] Shiv Sena contested elections with BJP and then formed a govt as Maha Vikas Aghadi.”Criticising INDIA, the central opposition bloc, he said it was a “10-headed Ravana” and should be destroyed. “They claim to be for the Constitution but they are anti-democracy,” he said.Shinde criticised Congress MP and leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi for leading a march to Supreme Court to submit petitions seeking an independent probe into allegations of arbitrary use of power by chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and suspension of the special intensive revision process. “It was an insult to the institution and the Constitution,” said Shinde.He also accused the opposition of trying to mislead the youth because it has lost its own following. “The opposition is creating chaos and is a traitor, but the public is wise and will not fall for this. This is not Nepal, Bangladesh or Pakistan,” said Shinde.
Article Summary: Eknath Shinde dedicated Shiv Sena’s annual Dussehra rally to drought-affected farmers. He said farmers have the first right over him and he will work for them ‘till the last drop of my blood’ He said Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah had also ensured their strong support.

Article Title: HC quashes suicide abetment case against man accused of telling debtor to ‘go die’
Article Text:
Aurangabad bench of Bombay high court

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Aurangabad bench of Bombay high court has quashed an abetment-to-suicide case against a man accused of telling a debtor to “go die” if he could not repay borrowed money, holding that the material on record did not prima facie establish the offence under sections 306 and 34 of IPC.Justice Sushil M Ghodeswar allowed a criminal revision application filed by Balaji Kishanrao Patil, setting aside a May 13, 2026, order of a Nanded sessions court that had rejected his plea for discharge.The case stemmed from the May 13, 2023, suicide of Sunil Ingole. Three days later, his widow lodged an FIR at Vimantal police station in Nanded, naming six people under sections 306 (abetment of suicide) and 34 (common intention) of Indian Penal Code (IPC).A suicide note left by Ingole named Shivaji Lakade and Pundlik Deshmukh of Chikhali, alleging harassment over money. Investigators also recovered a photograph of a handwritten chit in Marathi language from Ingole’s phone, which stated that Patil had been demanding repayment and had allegedly told him to “go die” if he had no money.Appearing for Patil, advocate Shivanand Tekwad argued that his client’s role was no different from that of the co-accused whose prosecutions had already been quashed.The chit merely showed that Patil had lent money and sought its repayment, which could not amount to abetment, he submitted. Ingole had not directly blamed Patil for his death in the suicide note, Tekwad submitted.The prosecution opposed the plea, contending that sufficient material existed to put Patil on trial.HC, however, noted that proceedings against co-accused Lakade and Pundlik Marotrao Ingole alias Deshmukh had already been quashed on Aug 7, 2025, while another accused, Saiprasad alias Sai Tukaram Sontakke, had secured similar relief on April 21, 2025.Relying on Supreme Court judgments in Mahendra Awase, M Mohan, Sanju alias Sanjay Singh Sengar and Ramesh Kumar, the court reiterated that mere harassment or casual remarks, without a positive act directly linked to the suicide, did not constitute abetment. It further observed that words spoken in anger or frustration, without an intention to provoke suicide, could not automatically be treated as instigation.The court held that the sessions judge had failed to properly apply these settled legal principles. The alleged “go die” remark, it said, had to be evaluated in the context of the overall circumstances and the evidence available on record.Observing that forcing Patil to face a criminal trial “in the teeth of the evidence available” would amount to an abuse of the process of law, HC granted him parity with the co-accused and quashed the proceedings against him.
Article Summary: Balaji Kishanrao Patil was accused of telling a debtor to “go die” if he could not repay borrowed money. The case stemmed from the May 13, 2023, suicide of Sunil Ingole. The court held that the material on record did not prima facie establish the offence.

Article Title: Demolition process begins within 24 hours of beef seizure from illegal slaughterhouse in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Authorities moved swiftly against an alleged illegal slaughterhouse in Rajeray Takli village of Khuldabad taluka, initiating demolition proceedings within 24 hours of seizing beef worth over Rs 1 lakh from the premises.The action began early on Sunday after police received a tip-off around 6 am about illegal cattle slaughter and sale of beef from a tin shed in Bazaar Galli. Dial 112 personnel were immediately dispatched to verify the information.After confirming the tip-off, a police team led by inspector Prashant Mahajan, along with sub-inspector Rajesh Patil and other personnel, raided the premises and seized meat from four slaughtered bovines. A panchnama was conducted on the spot.The matter was simultaneously brought to the notice of revenue and rural development authorities. By Tuesday, the block development officer had issued a notice, setting in motion the process to demolish the structure allegedly used for illegal slaughter.Superintendent of Police Prakash Jadhav said the administration acted without delay after the offence came to light. “Our teams seized beef of the slaughtered cattle and the matter was immediately brought to the notice of the BDO and tehsildar.The authorities concerned have since initiated the procedure to remove the structure allegedly used for illegal slaughter,” he said.Assistant SP Aparajita Agnihotri said the action formed part of a broader drive against illegal cattle slaughter and strict enforcement of the law. She said police were coordinating with other departments for further action in the case.According to police, Dial 112 personnel Ganesh Ghuge and Anil Rajput first verified the information and alerted the Khuldabad police station. The police team then moved in and conducted the raid.Mahajan said veterinary officials collected samples of the seized meat for forensic examination. “The veterinary officer collected meat samples for forensic examination. The remaining meat was destroyed in the presence of panch witnesses on government land along the Takli-Lamangaon road in Rajeray Takli village,” he said.Police have registered a case against three people.The FIR invokes sections 325 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, along with Sections 5(B), 5(C) and 6 of the Maharashtra Animal Preservation Act.
Article Summary: The action began early on Sunday after police received a tip-off about illegal cattle slaughter and sale of beef from a tin shed in Bazaar Galli. By Tuesday, the block development officer had issued a notice, setting in motion the process to demolish the structure allegedly used for illegal slaughter.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 2 women escape from RPF lockup in Navi Mumbai; 1 held after 6 hours, cop suspended
Article Text:
The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. (AI image)





NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: Ulhasnagar social activist Haresh Gajwani shot dead outside railway station, 3 arrested
Article Text:
Haresh Gajwani was murdered outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday night.





ULHASNAGAR: Police have arrested three suspects in connection with the murder of social worker Haresh Gajwani, who was shot dead outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday night. The suspects have been identified as Avinash Naidu, Vijay Singh and Noor Alam Khan.According to preliminary investigations, Gajwani and Naidu had a long-standing dispute. In 2021, counter-cases were registered against the two sides following a dispute, which allegedly contributed to continuing tensions between Gajwani and the accused.Police said the three suspects were traced and detained with the help of CCTV footage. Investigators are examining the alleged past rivalry, along with other possible motives behind the murder.Gajwani, 54, was allegedly attacked by three assailants who fired two rounds at him before fleeing the scene. Locals and police took him to Central Hospital, where doctors declared him "brought dead".Recently, Gajwani had posted on X, tagging senior officials from various police departments, as well as the chief minister, deputy chief minister and FDA commissioner Tukaram Mundhe. In his posts, he had highlighted alleged illegal activities in the area and claimed that some police personnel were supporting those involved. He had also expressed fears for his life, warning that the police personnel he had accused would also be responsible if anything happened to him.
Article Summary: Haresh Gajwani, 54, was shot dead outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday. Police have arrested three suspects in connection with the murder. The suspects have been identified as Avinash Naidu, Vijay Singh and Noor Alam Khan. Investigators are examining the alleged past rivalry, along with other possible motives.

Article Title: Grads’ Poll: Mahayuti Manifesto Focuses On Edu And Job Opportunities In Vidarbha
Article Text:
Mahayuti releases manifesto at Nagpur press event

Nagpur:





The Mahayuti manifesto released on Monday for the Nagpur graduates’ constituency election is built around eight areas with emphasis on education and job opportunities for graduates of entire Vidarbha.The manifesto was released by state revenue minister and Nagpur guardian minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule and Union minister of state Ramdas Athawale . It covers education and skill development, jobs and digital skills, women graduates, district-wise job sectors across Vidarbha, dialogue with graduates, an accountable system, and foreign education, fellowships and international jobs. BJP ’s Sudhakar Kohale is the alliance candidate. Bawankule said the seat carried special weight in the Legislative Council. “More than 2.5 lakh graduates will get their future issues solved through the legislature, and that is what makes this election important. Work on these areas has already begun under the Devendra Fadnavis and Narendra Modi govts, but it is our responsibility to get justice for the unemployed and graduates of Vidarbha,” he said.He said the document was not meant to end with polling day. “After six years we will give people an account of what we promised and what we did,” Bawankule said.The minister argued that Kohale would have the backing of govts at both the Centre and the state. “Whatever graduates’ issues Kohale raises in the House or brings to the govt, we have the capacity to resolve all of them,” he said.He said earlier MLCs such as the late Gangadhar Fadnavis, Union minister Nitin Gadkari and former MLC Anil Sole had kept their word. “A vote for Kohale is a vote that solves graduates’ problems. A vote for Congress is useful only for slogans, protests and going home,” said Bawankule on Congress candidate Abhijit Wanjarri, who won the seat in 2020.Kohale said the votes he is seeking are a loan which he will repay through his work. Bawankule said, “CM Devendra Fadnavis made a commitment that the govt will do whatever it needs to do to meet graduates’ expectations. Being guardian minister and revenue minister, I am also answerable for the promise Kohale has made here. We will take forward whatever issues the graduates raise,” he said.
Article Summary: Mahayuti manifesto built around eight areas with emphasis on education and job opportunities for graduates of Vidarbha. The manifesto was released by state revenue minister and Nagpur guardian minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule and Union minister of state Ramdas Athawale. BJP ’s Sudhakar Kohale is the alliance candidate.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Arms exhibition to mark Police Martyrs Memorial Day
Article Text:
Madurai

:





ClearedMadurai district police organised an arms exhibition on Tuesday as part of the observance of Police Martyrs Memorial Day.According to police, the exhibition aims to create awareness about the weapons and equipment used by the police force and highlight the services and sacrifices of police personnel in safeguarding society.The exhibition was held at the Armed Reserve Office in Madurai from 10am to 6pm and was attended by school students and the general public.Deputy Inspector General of Police, Madurai Range, Abhinav Kumar , inaugurated the exhibition.
Article Summary: Madurai district police organised an arms exhibition on Tuesday as part of the observance of Police Martyrs Memorial Day. The exhibition was held at the Armed Reserve Office in Madurai from 10am to 6pm and was attended by school students and the general public.

Article Title: Man dies after falling from tree in Madurai
Article Text:
Man dies after falling from tree in Madurai

Madurai

:





A 47-year-old man died after falling from a tree while cutting branches near Kalavasal Bypass Road in Madurai on Sunday.The deceased, Vijayakumar of Thirumangalam, was working near a ration shop off Kalavasal Bypass Road when he reportedly slipped and fell from a height equivalent to a two-storey building.He sustained severe injuries and was being rushed to a private hospital by his co-workers when he died on the way.SS Colony police registered a case and are investigating.
Article Summary: Vijayakumar of Thirumangalam was working near a ration shop. He reportedly slipped and fell from a height equivalent to a two-storey building. He sustained severe injuries and was being rushed to a private hospital by his co-workers when he died on the way.

Article Title: Tirunelveli police seize 600 tablets, arrest three
Article Text:
Tirunelveli police seize 600 tablets, arrest three

Tirunelveli:





Police seized 600 tablets of tapentadol and nitrazepam and arrested three people, while a juvenile was taken into protective custody, for allegedly possessing the medicines illegally for use as intoxicants.Acting on a tip-off, police intercepted four people standing suspiciously near the IIPE school bus stop, within the limits of the Tirunelveli Taluk police station, on Saturday. They were identified as Rishikesh , 19, and Vijay Aadithan, 22, both from Chennai; Janakiraman , 21, from Arakkonam; and a juvenile from Chennai.During a search, police allegedly found 600 tablets packed in 60 strips. The medicines are meant for medical use only on the recommendation of a registered medical practitioner.The Tirunelveli Taluk police registered a case and arrested the three adults, who were remanded in judicial custody. The juvenile was taken into protective custody, and further proceedings are under way under the provisions of the Juvenile Justice Act.
Article Summary: Police seized 600 tablets of tapentadol and nitrazepam and arrested three people. A juvenile was taken into protective custody for allegedly possessing the medicines illegally for use as intoxicants. The medicines are meant for medical use only on the recommendation of a registered medical practitioner.

Article Title: Traffic affected on Salem-Madurai National Highway after trailer truck crashes near Rasipuram
Article Text: NAMAKKAL: Traffic was affected for more than an hour on the Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram in Namakkal district on Thursday afternoon after a trailer truck crashed while descending the Andagalur Gate flyover.No casualties or injuries were reported.The truck was carrying about 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. An officer at the Rasipuram police station said the driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover around 1.30pm. The truck hit a streetlight pole on the roadside. “The vehicle partially blocked the road, causing congestion and delays for motorists and commuters,” he said.Vehicles piled up for two kilometres on the NH. The Rasipuram police reached the spot after receiving information, regulated traffic and moved the truck to the roadside.Police registered a case and were investigating the circumstances leading to the crash.
Article Summary: Trailer truck crashes on Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram. Truck was carrying 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. Driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover. No casualties or injuries were reported.

Article Title: Amid row over CMRL stance, flex boards with Oommen Chandy’s photo appear in Kottayam
Article Text:
File photo of late CM Oommen Chandy and leader of opposition Pinarayi Vijayan

Kottayam

:





Flex boards carrying the photograph of former chief minister Oommen Chandy have appeared in Kottayam, amid criticism that the state govt had taken a soft stance in the high court towards leader of opposition Pinarayi Vijayan in the CMRL–Exalogic case.The boards, put up in the name of Congress workers, were first seen near the Gandhi statue and later at several other locations, including in front of Kottayam Press Club. Addressed to Vijayan, they say party workers have not forgotten what was done to Chandy.The boards come as unease grows in Congress over the govt’s stance in the high court in the case. MLA Mathew Kuzhalnadan was the first to publicly criticise the stance, followed by Congress‘s Jinto John.Meanwhile, Chandy Oommen responded that his father had not got justice, but that using this as a pretext to target another person was not the Congress way.
Article Summary: The boards, put up in the name of Congress workers, were first seen near the Gandhi statue and later at several other locations. Addressed to Vijayan, they say party workers have not forgotten what was done to Chandy. Comes as unease grows in Congress over the govt’s stance in the high court in the case.
